newsitem.title: UK: UK GOVT SEES INFLATION HITTING TARGET SOON.
newsitem.headline: UK GOVT SEES INFLATION HITTING TARGET SOON.

text.p: Junior British Treasury minister Geoffrey Robinson said on Tuesday he expected underlying inflation to drop back to the government's target within the next couple of months.
"I think we can look forward to it being on target within the next couple of months," he told BBC radio.
The government has a target of 2.5 percent for annual inflation excluding mortgage interest payments.
Inflation would fall "as we get some of the benefits from the budget on the disinflationary side," Robinson, who is Paymaster General, said.
Official figures out on Tuesday showed underlying inflation leapt to 3.0 percent in the year to July, from 2.7 percent in June.

That was largely due to hefty petrol and oil price rises following duty increases in Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's first budget, and mortgage rate rises in response to a series of interest rate hikes.
Robinson said Brown's July 2 was tough enough and bore down heavily on consumer spending.
"We tackled mortgage interest rates, we tackled the cost of petrol and of course it's the cost of petrol that this month has given the increase we see at the moment," he said.

"Next month...we will get the benefit of the cut in VAT on fuel. We are confident we will see inflation coming down over the next few months, very much in line with the target we set." Brown's budget cut VAT on heating fuel to five percent from eight, the lowest level allowable under European Union rules.
